## Summary

Uses the existing Sepo GitHub auth resolver before posting preview URLs, so preview comments come from the Sepo agent GitHub App/token instead of the default `github-actions[bot]` token when Sepo auth is available.

The workflow still falls back to `${{ github.token }}` if Sepo app/OIDC auth is unavailable.

## Notes

- The exact visible author is determined by the installed GitHub App slug. In this repo that should show as the Sepo agent app bot rather than `github-actions[bot]`.
- Existing `github-actions[bot]` preview comments may not be edited by the new identity; future preview runs should update the Sepo-authored comment.

## Test plan

- [x] `actionlint .github/workflows/preview.yml`

Here is the synthesis. --- ## Summary of PR/Issue PR #68 makes the `preview.yml` workflow post its "Sepo preview: " comment as the Sepo agent identity instead of `github-actions[bot]`. It does this by inserting a `Resolve Sepo agent auth` step that reuses the existing [`resolve-github-auth`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/action.yml) composite action, then swapping the `Comment URL` step's `GH_TOKEN` from `${{ github.token }}` to the resolved `steps.auth.outputs.token`. The auth step is gated by `if: steps.deploy.outputs.url != ''` (matching the comment step), so no token is minted when there's nothing to post, and `github.token` remains the fallback. It's a 9-line, single-file change that reuses an established repo pattern rather than rebuilding token handling. ## Review The change is correct, well-scoped, and achieves its goal on this repo's primary GitHub App path; one minor consistency gap is worth fixing before merge. The rubrics reviewer returned N/A (no `agent/rubrics` branch configured), so all substantive findings come from the code review. | Issue | Severity | Description | | -- | -- | -- | | Omits `pat` input — only call site of 22 that does | WARNING | In app-less + OIDC-broker-down + PAT-configured setups, the comment falls back to `github-actions[bot]` instead of the Sepo PAT identity, undercutting the PR goal and breaking cross-workflow parity. | | Auth-step failure now gates the preview comment | INFO | If app creds are set but invalid (or only one of the two is set), the `auth` step hard-fails and no comment is posted — a mild robustness regression vs. the prior unconditional path, only on misconfigured secrets. | | Transitional duplicate comment | INFO | On PRs with an existing `github-actions[bot]` preview comment, the first run under the new identity posts a fresh Sepo comment and orphans the old one. Self-heals; acknowledged in the PR body. | | `--edit-last` under app token unverified | INFO | `preview.yml` is the only workflow using `gh pr comment --edit-last`; sticky-edit behavior under the app identity should be confirmed on first live run. The `||` fallback prevents job failure regardless. | ## Progress - **Transitional duplicate comment** is already disclosed in the PR description — intentionally accepted, no action expected. - **Rubrics review:** N/A — no `agent/rubrics` branch exists for this repo, so rubric scoring was skipped (a scoping outcome, not a quality judgment). Optional follow-up: run **Agent / Rubrics / Initialization** if rubric steering is desired. - **Inline comment posted:** one new same-agent inline comment on `.github/workflows/preview.yml:59` ([discussion_r3358268528](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/pull/68#discussion_r3358268528)) with an applyable suggestion adding the `pat` line. No prior inline comments or review threads existed, so nothing was replied to, resolved, or minimized. - **Design confirmed sound:** token is masked inside the action; required permissions (`id-token: write`, `pull-requests: write`) are already granted at the workflow level; `actionlint` passed per the PR test plan. ## Issue Details
Omits pat input — only call site of 22 that does **Cause:** The new `with:` block passes `app_id`, `app_private_key`, and `fallback_token` but not `pat`. Every one of the 22 other `resolve-github-auth` invocations in `.github/workflows/` passes the full `app_id → app_private_key → pat → fallback_token` chain (31 occurrences confirmed by grep). The action's resolution order ([action.yml:81-96](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/action.yml)) is `github_app → oidc_broker (only when app creds empty) → pat → github_token`. **Candidate solutions:** Add `pat: ${{ secrets.AGENT_PAT }}` after the `app_private_key` input (line 59). One-line change; restores parity with all sibling workflows and preserves the Sepo identity in PAT-only fallback setups. **Comments:** Non-blocking — in this repo's primary config the app token wins and `pat` is never consulted, so the happy path is unaffected. The gap only manifests when app creds are absent **and** the OIDC broker fails **and** a PAT is configured, where the comment would post as `github-actions[bot]` rather than the Sepo machine user. Safe for an automated fix.
Auth-step failure now gates the preview comment **Cause:** The `Comment URL` step previously used `github.token` directly and was independent of any auth resolution. Now it depends on the `auth` step, which hard-fails if `create-github-app-token@v1` rejects invalid app creds, or if exactly one of `app_id`/`app_private_key` is set (the action's validation step). With no `if: always()` on `Comment URL`, a failed `auth` step turns the job red and posts no comment. **Candidate solutions:** Acceptable as-is given it only triggers on misconfigured secrets. If extra robustness is wanted, the comment step could tolerate auth failure, but that adds complexity for a low-probability misconfiguration and isn't recommended for this PR.
Transitional duplicate comment **Cause:** On a PR that already has a `github-actions[bot]` preview comment, the first run under the Sepo identity finds no Sepo-authored comment, so `--edit-last` fails and the `||` fallback posts a new Sepo comment, leaving the old one orphaned. **Candidate solutions:** None required — self-heals for new PRs and is explicitly acknowledged in the PR description. Reviewers should just expect a one-time double comment on in-flight PRs.
--edit-last under app token unverified **Cause:** `preview.yml` is the only workflow using `gh pr comment --edit-last`. Sticky-edit worked under `github-actions[bot]` (itself an app), and an app installation token resolves `viewer` the same way, so editing *should* continue in place — but it hasn't been exercised under the Sepo app in this repo. **Candidate solutions:** No code change needed. Confirm operationally on the first live agent PR that a second push edits the same comment rather than appending. The `||` fallback guarantees the job won't fail even in the worst case.
## Recommended Next Step `FIX_PR` — adding `pat: ${{ secrets.AGENT_PAT }}` is a mechanical, one-line change that exactly matches 22 sibling call sites, has no downside on the primary path, and is safe for an automated fix-pr pass. ## Final Verdict `MINOR_ISSUES` ## Action Items - [ ] In the `Resolve Sepo agent auth` step's `with:` block, add `pat: ${{ secrets.AGENT_PAT }}` after `app_private_key` (`.github/workflows/preview.yml:59`) to match all 22 other `resolve-github-auth` call sites and preserve the Sepo identity in PAT-only fallback configs. --- `claude` | `default` | `max` | `GitHub Actions 1000001675`
